title: | Sabbath Morning: the Fall of Replacement Theology

sense.text:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” Everything written beforetime was written for our learning, and we are a people that have to re-learn who we are, because of the atrocities that have happened to us as a people and continue to happen to us up until this day.

The difference now is that what happens to us has become so regular that we have normalized it: the oppression, the racial profiling, the miseducation, and we just say ‘that’s the black experience, that’s how life is for black people.’

If you don’t study and master the Old Testament you will not learn what the New Testament is about. You will believe things like replacement theology, believe it wholeheartedly, and die in it, sitting in church your whole life thinking you’re a Gentile.

What other race is told by society to forget their past? They never told the Jewish people to forget the Holocaust; they never told the Asian people to forget the times they were held in camps; it’s in all their movies. That is why we have to relearn this Bible: it comes from these scriptures.

When it comes to learning you have to make sure you are taught right, because you can learn this Bible wrong. “But the word of the Lord was unto them precept upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line”: they were reading the Bible the same exact way as the ones God said he would teach, precept upon precept, “that they might go, and fall backward, and be broken, and snared, and taken.”

They read it the same way but they did not get the same understanding; they did not learn the Bible right. That is your modern Christians today, your pastors, your Muslim imams and the rest. They have read the Bible and said it was made up, that it is the Egyptian scrolls or the Gilgamesh epics, that God loves everybody, that Jesus was not the son of God but just a prophet. They read it the same way and fell backward because they learned wrong.

precepts.why:
To compare and contrast, jump up to verses 9 and 10. “Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand doctrine? them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts.” Those are the ones that are reborn … he’ll make them understand.

“For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line”: these will be taught precept upon precept and they will get the understanding.

So verse 10 and verse 13 describe the same way of reading, but verse 10 is the ones God teaches, who get the understanding, and verse 13 is the ones who read it the same way and fall backward, broken, snared and taken.

sense.text:
We have to take our learning seriously in these last days. If you think Satan is just going to step back and say ‘come on down this narrow road and walk right into the kingdom,’ no: he is going to make it difficult. It is going to be an all-out war against the truth.

“Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.” You have to study to show yourself approved to God, so that God gives you the spirit of discernment. You have to be able to study, discern and divide up the word: what is the context here, what does this mean here, what does that mean there. Otherwise you just take scriptures like John 3:16 and equate them to everybody, and that is what has happened.

These are the basic scriptures gone over a lot, because many new people are finding out, through the mouth of the prophets, that God is revealing to them who they are. They are coming into this truth and need to know these things so they can build upon them as a babe and be taught.

“Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read”: that is what you have to study. Sure, other books get used, like a compact Bible dictionary, but those didn’t come until the book of the Lord was studied thoroughly. When it comes to studying you have to read the main source, or the other sources will confuse you and you will bring their understanding into the book of the Lord.

Many of us have been deceived because we don’t read, especially in Christianity. A lack of reading has caused us to be deceived. God says seek ye out of the book of the Lord and read, but we won’t read; we turn on a video and sit there staring at the pastor, and that is how you get deceived. People in the truth do it too, sitting there staring at the screen just listening. You have to read along.

“No one of these shall fail, none shall want her mate: for my mouth it hath commanded, and his spirit it hath gathered them.” You have to seek out the book of the Lord so you are not deceived, and read it precept upon precept as it is supposed to be read.

“This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night.” That is why Bishop gave us the formula: four chapters a day. You don’t have to read all four at one sitting. We have jobs, we’re busy, we wake up early and we’re tired at night, so break it up: two chapters in the morning when you wake up, two on your lunch break or in the evening. Start your day with the word, meditating in it when you wake up and when you go to sleep. Read two chapters out of the law in the morning and two somewhere else, in the gospels or the prophets, wherever you are studying. That is a minimum of four a day; you might read six or eight. There is no excuse. As long as you are meditating therein day and night, because Satan is out there day and night.

“That thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.” This is Joshua.

The book called The Icon has an image of King David, and King David is black. Notice that first and don’t look past his color like you don’t see it, Christians: you see his black ass face and black hands. ‘Oh his color doesn’t matter.’ Shut up. God made you see in color for a reason; if color didn’t matter you would be colorblind like a dog.

And look at the big old Bible he is holding. There is a reason that when they drew King David they put a humongous Bible in his hand: David liked to meditate on the word of God that much.

precepts.why:
You have to meditate day and night because Satan is out there day and night: “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour.”

Satan is a spiritual being. He doesn’t need sleep and rest like us, he doesn’t take breaks, he doesn’t know what tired feels like. So he is seeking whom he may devour, those who don’t study to show themselves approved to God, and therefore they are deceived. It might be something on TV, something they come across, or just the thought, ‘man, I’m doing all right without even reading the Bible, you don’t even need it, just go about your life and get money.’ Boom, got you. He plants that thought in your mind, lets it fester until it comes to fruition, and you run with it.

If you have been in the truth a while, go back and watch the movie Constantine. They took stuff right out of the Bible and made a movie of it, and if you look at it from a spiritual aspect and not just for enjoyment, you’ll see how Satan goes to and fro and plants a thought in your mind.

See what David did: “I will meditate in thy precepts, and have respect unto thy ways.” David wasn’t just trying to read and get his chapters a day out of the way; he was meditating on the precepts.

“I will delight myself in thy statutes.” That is the reason they drew King David with a humongous Bible in his hand: David loved reading the book of the Lord.

And the one time he put the book of the Lord down, he went and found Bathsheba, looking at her, and got caught slipping, because Satan was roaming about seeking whom he may devour. From the kings down to the peasants, Satan doesn’t care.

Here is the law on it, what the kings had to do: “And it shall be, when he sitteth upon the throne of his kingdom, that he shall write him a copy of this law in a book out of that which is before the priests the Levites.” So King David wrote out the Bible, what he had at the time, the laws of Moses, since the Psalms were still being written over time.

“And it shall be with him, and he shall read therein all the days of his life: that he may learn to fear the Lord his God, to keep all the words of this law and these statutes, to do them.” There you go: the king had to read the law all the days of his life, meditating in it day and night.

sense.text:
This is gone through because replacement theology has come through the lack of studying on our part as a people. See what David said: “O how love I thy law!” David loved the law of the Most High. A lot of us neglect the laws of God and read just the prophets and the gospels; we meditate in Sirach and read the Ezras but neglect the law. ‘I ain’t read it in a while.’ Why? Read what King David said.

“It is my meditation all the day.” That means you have to make time for the laws of God and study them. Yes, you’re busy, but you can’t keep using that excuse, because you make time for other stuff.

None of you is busier than King David. The king runs a country, cities; everything goes to the king, and he has to be aware and knowledgeable of everything. None of us is running countries right now; that comes in time. David had to be in the know of everything and he still found time for the Most High’s word, and he says to you, it is my meditation all the day. So we have no excuse. ‘I ain’t got no time’: you can’t say that in the eyes of God.
“Thou through thy commandments hast made me wiser than mine enemies: for they are ever with me.” God will make you wiser than your enemies, than those that try to cast you down for what you believe.

“I have more understanding than all my teachers: for thy testimonies are my meditation. I understand more than the ancients.” Those teachers today would be your biblical scholars, your pastors, your apologists. Go through the precepts and meditate, and you’ll get more understanding of the Bible than them without ever going to a Bible school.

Watch the video from IUIC New Orleans with Officer Matthew. He has never been to a Bible school or a theology school, and look how he dismantled a pastor: with a monotone voice, very soft spoken, taking his time, and the pastor was flabbergasted. He could not handle the basic questions Officer Matthew was asking. You get more understanding than all your teachers, than the scholars.

precepts.why:
You have to make time for it, and Sirach says why: “The wisdom of a learned man cometh by opportunity of leisure.” Wisdom comes by opportunity of leisure, so you have to clear your schedule. “And he that hath little business shall become wise.”

Then it asks how he can get wisdom that holds the plough and drives oxen and is occupied in their labours, whose talk is always about work. It is always about money. You ever notice that people can never study the Bible because they are always trying to chase the bag and get money?

Yet none of you is busier than King David, and he said the law is my meditation all the day.

sense.text:
“Through thy precepts I get understanding: therefore I hate every false way.” Through the precepts, from the Old Testament to the New Testament, you get understanding, and therefore you will hate every false way, like Christianity.

We have been church blitzing, and we don’t hate our brothers in Christianity; we hate the establishment of Christianity, because it is a false way. It is a false way of living, a false way of understanding God, a false way of understanding Christ, a false way of putting forth who the people of God are. The establishment of Christianity is of the devil.

If you don’t understand through the precepts you will begin to say things like ‘God now chose everybody, we are all God’s people, we are all God’s children, God loves everybody, God made everybody.’ We have heard that stuff before, brothers and sisters. They lack understanding.

precepts.why:
Basic stuff, so you can understand: “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.” You have to fear God, that he will judge you for the wrong you do.

That understanding comes when stuff happens in your life. You don’t just pass it off as ‘I’m going through a rough patch, that’s just how things is,’ luck or happy chance. Those are the little amendments God is doing in your life, trying to bring you back to fearing him, so he can begin to impart wisdom upon you.

“A good understanding have all they that do his commandments.” Doing the commandments is where you begin to get the understanding, because then God sees that you respect his word. The fear of the Lord goes into the respect of the Lord: knowing he can do whatever he wants to you and take your life in a moment. Then God says, okay, I can deal with them, I can begin to impart wisdom and understanding upon them.

“My flesh trembleth for fear of thee; and I am afraid of thy judgments.” There you go: David was afraid of God’s judgments.

So how is it that the damn warehouse shop worker, the receptionist, the thotty, the bad b, don’t fear the Lord, when King David said I fear God?

sense.text:
There are some ways to learn. “So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.” Hearing the word of God is also a way of learning the things that were written aforetime, but it cannot replace reading.

Many have come into this truth and don’t like reading. That is not about those who have problems reading, who haven’t learned to read well or have a disability that keeps them from reading or comprehending well; that is different. It is about those with a sound mind who don’t like picking up the book of the Lord. You can listen to the word, but it can’t replace reading. That is why God says seek ye out of the book and read; David meditated: read, read, read.

Hearing only reaffirms what you have already read. It is like a double scoop: you read it, then you hear it, and it sticks more. You can’t just hear and hear and hear, because it won’t stick. There is something about seeing it, reading it and hearing it yourself that makes it stick. It is a process.

“Neither have I gone back from the commandment of his lips; I have esteemed the words of his mouth more than my necessary food.” Job said the words of the Most High are more important than his food.

We have to get to that level in the spirit, where we dedicate ourselves: ‘first thing I’m doing is studying; breakfast can wait. I’m intermittent fasting, I need to shed some body fat, I’ll eat a little later. The first thing I’m putting into my spirit is the word of God.’ Our dedication to study has to get to where we seek out the word more than anything.

Look what God did with Ezekiel. “But thou, son of man, hear what I say unto thee; Be not thou rebellious like that rebellious house.” How was that rebellious house? You won’t read, you won’t seek out the book of the Lord: rebellious like our brothers in Christianity, who live their life six, seven days a week, and church is just a bump in the road during the week. Black folk go there just to sing and dance and go about their way. Football season is about to start back up, and the black men that go to church right now aren’t worried about that damn church; they only go to hear the song and then get out so they can go watch the Cowboys game on Fox. That was done in the world, but we can’t be rebellious like that.

“Open thy mouth, and eat that I give thee.” God is telling Ezekiel to eat. Eat what?
“And when I looked, behold, an hand was sent unto me; and, lo, a roll of a book was therein.” That is the Bible, a roll of a book, right there, and God told him to eat it.

“And he spread it before me”: he opened up the book. “And it was written within and without”, front and back, “and there was written therein lamentations, and mourning, and woe.” And God told him to eat that. What does that mean? Study that thing, get it into your soul.

precepts.why:
The chapters are divided for us, but this is a continuation of the same thought of what God said to eat. “Moreover he said unto me, Son of man, eat that thou findest; eat this roll”: take all this Bible in. “And go speak unto the house of Israel.”

You can’t speak to God’s people until you have had a good serving of the word of God: eaten it, digested it, taken it in and meditated on it. Otherwise you will tell the people of God they are Gentiles, that it doesn’t matter what race you are in the eyes of God, and you’ll be confident in your stupidity.

“So I opened my mouth, and he caused me to eat that roll. And he said unto me, Son of man, cause thy belly to eat, and fill thy bowels with this roll that I give thee.” That’s cold-blooded: get your belly full of the word of God.

“Then did I eat it; and it was in my mouth as honey for sweetness.” It was sweet to him, and that is how it is for all of us when we find out we are Israel. The word has to be sweet to us; we have to love it and it has to taste good, even the history that a lot of us don’t like reading. When I first came in it was so sweet: reading the law, when I found out the dietary law, I highlighted the whole chapter of Leviticus 11 in orange in my first Bible. It was the spirit of the Lord.

sense.text: “Therefore take no thought, saying, What shall we eat?” Don’t take thought about the physical food of the earth; you have other food you need to be eating and digesting and getting in your belly right now.

“But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.” With all the temptations and distractions of this world, Christ told us the main thing to focus on to survive and make it through, so they don’t draw us out to the wide road that leads to destruction.

The wide road that leads to destruction and the narrow road that leads to life are side by side. As you walk the narrow road you will see the temptations and distractions on the wide road, all of them saying come over here: ‘free before 11, all women.’ Your family will be over there waving at you: ‘come on over here, it’s granny’s birthday, granny ain’t did no wrong to you, don’t do your family like that.’ That is what is going to be going on.

But Christ told you what to focus on the most: focus on the word of God, eat that thing.

precepts.why:
Here is more proof of it. “But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone.” Look at what Christ is telling you about that physical bread that we as a people lust after so. How many people have you met who say ‘oh, I love food, I love to eat out’? Some in the truth take it that way too.

“But by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.” That is your food, your spiritual food: the words that feed our spirit more than the physical. That is what you have to focus on and take in.

“In the mean while his disciples prayed him, saying, Master, eat.” Master, here, eat some food; we’ve been out teaching the word of God all day, I know you’re hungry. Look what Christ said: “I have meat to eat”. Man, I have to teach the people, I can’t take a break eating, so many people need to hear the word of God; I have food you don’t know anything about, I’m not worried about that physical food.

“Therefore said the disciples one to another, Hath any man brought him ought to eat? Jesus saith unto them, My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work.”

What is the will God told us to do? Seek ye out of the book of the Lord and read; meditate therein day and night; study to show thyself approved. You might not be a street teacher, a captain, a bishop, a deacon, an officer or a soldier, but you still have a will of God that he wants you to do: to eat up. Those are the steps to learning: make it that important to you, or you will find yourself caught up in replacement theology.

sense.text:
Replacement theology, also called supersessionism, teaches that the church has replaced Israel in God’s plan, and that the promises made to Israel are fulfilled in the Christian church. That’s why you get ‘spiritual Israel’. The church they’re thinking of is the Baptist church, and ain’t no damn Baptist church in the bible. When Paul was establishing churches in the cities he travelled to, nowhere did he set up a Baptist church, nowhere a Methodist or Episcopalian church. Supersessionism says the new covenant has replaced the law of Moses; that’s why they say the law of Moses is done away with, which makes no sense, because you still live up under thou shalt not kill, and that’s the law of Moses. Replacement theology is Christianity. That’s why people that don’t even read the bible know John 3:16 and don’t know the ten commandments: it’s been pushed down from the world council of churches that they have replaced the people of God, the Israelites. There is only one group on the earth that teaches that the chosen people of God are still the Israelites. Today’s class sways both ways: people have tried to replace Israel in God’s plan, and there are also people out there that think we are trying to replace the people of God as Israelites. Replacement theology is going to take a fall.

They often claim supersessionism originated with Paul the apostle; this is where the lack of understanding of keeping the commandments came in. When Peter said the letters of Paul are hard to understand, he meant it. It’s not ‘just read it over and over again and you’ll get it’; it’s another level of hard to be understood.

“And account that the longsuffering of our Lord is salvation; even as our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you”. Just meditating on verse 15 you would understand it. Peter was sent to the southern kingdom, to the Israelites. So if Peter says Paul has written about salvation unto you, it’s already telling you who salvation is for.

“As also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things; in which are some things hard to be understood”. For Peter to say that means that when Peter read those letters he had to meditate, precept upon precept, searching the scriptures in the law and the prophets, the Torah and the Tanakh, to find out what Paul was talking about. It wasn’t that Peter read it and said, oh yeah, that’s easy. Peter read it and said, man, that could be confusing right there. Peter was the top, the head disciple; he read these letters before they went anywhere, and he saw that this was going to cause the unstable and the unlearned in the word of God to stumble.

“Which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest, as they do also the other scriptures, unto their own destruction.” The unlearned and the unstable will wrestle with the letters of Paul. For Peter to say that, there were already people out there stumbling and wrestling with the teachings and the letters of Paul in that day. Hence you got supersessionism and replacement theology.

precepts.why:
How do we know they were already stumbling in the time of Paul? He would write to a church, they would read it, and the unlearned would stumble over it. “What advantage then hath the Jew?” The Jew, that’s the southern kingdom. “Much every way”.

That pastor Geno Jennings thinks he’s the prophet of God, and he talks about the other pastors and the Israelites, but look how he reads it: what advantage then hath the Jew, or what profit is there of circumcision, and then he goes straight to verse nine. He didn’t read verse two. He read verse one and merged verse nine with it, and did not tell the people that he was in verse nine. That’s why we tell you, you got to study to show yourself approved, because when you hear it you’ll say, hold up, that don’t say that: right after verse one it says “Much every way”. To deceive the people into replacement theology you read verse one and merge verse nine with it. Geno Jennings ain’t nothing but replacement theology, supersessionism; that’s why he’s so mad at us, because we called him out on his damn lies.

“Much every way: chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God.” They grew up in the law.

This is the verse that was merged with verse one. “What then? are we better than they? No, in no wise: for we have before proved both Jews and Gentiles, that they are all under sin”. Here Paul is talking about the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom. It comes after the advantage of the Jew, not in place of it.

“For what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect?” Keep it in context: what if some didn’t believe that Christ was the Messiah that was foretold to come? Shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect? “God forbid”: it don’t matter if they believe it or not, it’s the truth.

“Yea, let God be true, but every man a liar; as it is written”. Paul is saying, the stuff I’m telling you about Christ being the Messiah, that we don’t have to sacrifice to be forgiven of our sins no more, that stuff is as it is written. The letters I’m writing to you are as it is written; you just don’t understand it. “That thou mightest be justified in thy sayings, and mightest overcome when thou art judged.”

This is how you know that when people heard the teachings of Paul or heard his letters read aloud, they were already stumbling at that time. “But if our unrighteousness commend the righteousness of God”: if Paul is out there calling the people back to God, why would he have to say our unrighteousness? Because the people didn’t understand the letters of Paul; it was beyond their understanding. Hence you got supersessionism and replacement theology.

“What shall we say? Is God unrighteous who taketh vengeance? (I speak as a man) God forbid: for then how shall God judge the world? For if the truth of God hath more abounded through my lie unto his glory; why yet am I also judged as a sinner?” If more people are repenting and returning to God through the so-called lie that I’m teaching, why am I judged as a sinner? It’s the same with us: these young men are coming up off the streets, these women are coming out the clubs, more people are repenting when they find out they Israelites, and why are we referred to as sinners? Because we’re destroying your lies of replacement theology.

“And not rather, (as we be slanderously reported, and as some affirm that we say,) Let us do evil, that good may come? whose damnation is just.” Paul was slanderously reported because they didn’t understand his writings; Peter told you it’s hard to be understood. Just like they do with us: they call us a hate group, nationalists, black Hebrew Israelites. Slanderously reported, because you don’t understand the bible, so you’re mad at us for destroying the lies that have been taught for centuries in Christianity.

Get some understanding on this. “Paul called the chief of the Jews together: and when they were come together, he said unto them, Men and brethren, though I have committed nothing against the people, or customs of our fathers”. So Paul was not going around teaching that you don’t have to keep the commandments no more. He was not going around teaching that the church, Baptist, Pentecostal, was going to replace Israel and that all people are the people of God now. So when you read Gentiles, that ain’t what Paul’s talking about: he said he committed nothing against the people or customs of the fathers.

“Yet was I delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans. Who, when they had examined me, would have let me go, because there was no cause of death in me. But when the Jews spake against it”: why were they speaking against it? Because they didn’t understand what Paul was writing.

“Because that for the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.” Paul is telling you, what I’m doing is the hope of Israel. I’ve received the understanding that this is the way to salvation; it’s been revealed to me, so I’m going to tell all Israel to return from their idolatry and come out of their sins. The Messiah has come; the doors of salvation are open unto us, not through Moses but through Jesus the Christ.

“As concerning this sect, we know that every where it is spoken against.” That sounds like the Israelites teaching today: everywhere it is spoken against. You saying everybody can’t be saved, that God don’t love everybody? We don’t want to hear that, don’t bring that here. It was spoken against everywhere because they didn’t understand what Paul was teaching: when he said we’re not under the law no more, we’re under grace, they said, what you talking about, not under the law, you tripping; talking about these other nations could be saved. As we see, Paul was teaching that his teachings were for the hope of Israel.

“Though he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered; And being made perfect, he became the author of eternal salvation unto all them that obey him”. All them of who? The house of Israel. He’s talking to the Hebrews here, not to everybody else: all them that obey him, that repent and turn from their sins, all the house of Israel.

“Called of God an high priest after the order of Melchisedec. Of whom we have many things to say, and hard to be uttered, seeing ye are dull of hearing.” Paul is telling the elders of Israel, those whose profession it is to study the law and the Torah every day and minister the word of God every day: you are dull of hearing, this is above you. Man, I’m talking about Melchizedek and equating it to Christ, and this is way above your head.

“For when for the time ye ought to be teachers”: they were already teachers, the elders of Israel. “Ye have need that one teach you again which be the first principles of the oracles of God”. He’s telling elders that have been teaching people for twenty, thirty, forty years: you need to keep on studying to show yourself approved. “And are become such as have need of milk, and not of strong meat.” This is how bad Paul was in the scriptures: he’s telling elders, you need to go back and learn the milk again, you need to be weaned from the breast; go back to the basics. Paul was a bad man; he’s schooling elders. So how in the hell do you expect black Christian pastors, and Hispanics caught up in Christianity, in a land that’s not theirs, with the last name of their slave masters, to possibly understand the letters of Paul, when Paul is telling the elders of Jerusalem to go back and study the basics?

“For every one that useth milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe.” Y’all don’t even know what you’re talking about when it comes to the real meaning of this law and the hard to be understood prophecies, when you’re teaching these people. “But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age”: to the elders, the bishops, the deacons. “Even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.” Paul is saying your understanding of the Messiah is a babe’s; you ain’t ready for the meat, you ain’t there yet.

The letters were hard to be understood, and when you teach the truth of God, people are going to hate you and come against you no matter what. Because God has given the bishops and the deacons, and their teachers before them, the understanding of the letters of Paul, and we have cast down the imaginations of the world of replacement theology and supersessionism, they now list Israel United in Christ as the number three largest hate group, with the ideology of ‘general hate’. What the hell does that mean?

sense.text:
Christianity says the old covenant is moral, ceremonial and civil, and that the ceremonial and the civil, the judicial laws of how to deal with one another in business and the punishments for breaking the law, are done away with. You know why they say the ceremonial is done away? Because the church keeps the ceremonies of America. They don’t celebrate passover, they celebrate Easter; they don’t celebrate tabernacles, they celebrate Halloween. They replaced those things with Thanksgiving, Presidents’ Day, St. Patrick’s Day, birthdays. This is well thought out evil, way above the average negro’s head.

Why don’t they keep the civil laws, like if you steal something from somebody you gotta do this, that and the other? Because they are fully engulfed in doing everything America tells them to do. Whatever law America passes, sodomy, transgenderism, gender fluid, they are fully in agreement with it: we’re going to follow all of the white man’s laws and disregard any of the laws of God. In this captivity, in Christianity, the white man is their god.

Then they say you only gotta keep the moral law of the ten commandments, and that binds you as a Christian believer. They don’t even do that. So compare and contrast it with the commandments themselves: “And God spake all these words”.

“I am the Lord thy God”: the Lord thy God of Israel. This is the exodus: “which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.” Egypt was bondage for us; they made us serve hard bondage building the pyramids in the valley of kings.

“Thou shalt have no other gods before me.” Remember, they say you don’t have to keep this, because technically this is not a moral law; the moral law starts at six on down. So according to replacement theology and the Christian church, you can worship other gods and receive the kingdom. You just gotta love the satanist, love those that love satan worship. That’s what Christian theology is saying, if you say the moral laws are the only things you got to keep.

“Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image”. So under their doctrine you can pray to an idol of whatever god you want to, be fully engulfed in making idols and praying to them, as long as you don’t sleep with another man’s wife.

precepts.why: Jump down the same chapter: “Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain; for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.” To take the name of the Lord thy God in vain is to break the commandments, embarrass him, do what you’re not supposed to do and put it on God, like these rappers do. Replacement theology says you can do that as long as you don’t bear false witness.

“Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work”. They’re saying you don’t have to keep the sabbath day holy as long as you don’t kill nobody. Christ kept the sabbath day holy, but Christians under replacement theology don’t have to do it no more.

So you can have another god, make idols, take God’s name in vain, not keep the sabbath day holy, not honor your parents, none of that, as long as you don’t kill, commit adultery, bear false witness or covet. That’s it. Let’s see if that’s true.

sense.text: “But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities”: our sins. “The chastisement of our peace was upon him”: our peace. Look, for those that are in the Christian doctrine: the good thing about God is that he clears up who he’s talking about, so you cannot generalize his words. As long as you read, you’ll understand who God is talking about.

“All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the Lord hath laid on him the iniquity of us all.” If you’re not reading and studying yourself, you would say, man, that’s everybody, it says us all. We are the world, we are the children: they used to try to make us sing that in damn elementary school, and that’s why you think it means everybody. But keep reading.

“For he was cut off out of the land of the living: for the transgression of my people was he stricken.” For the transgression of my people. See how God clears up that us all. God clears up the all as long as you keep reading, to study and to show yourself approved.

“Yet it pleased the Lord to bruise him; he hath put him to grief: when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see his seed”. That’s what was written of him to fulfill: to make his soul an offering for sin, so you won’t have to sacrifice no more. That’s what Paul was going to teach, but it was not revealed to those that did not study to show themselves approved, that wrestled with the other laws, that grew up under Greek ways eating pork, sacrificing to other gods and eating unclean animals. So when they read in the law thou shalt not eat swine, they said, man, I don’t have to do that no more; the Greeks rule over us.

That’s why Peter said they’re gonna wrestle with these letters just like they wrestle with the other laws. When Peter was out there teaching he was hearing: man, we can eat whatever we want to, eat things sacrificed to idols, eat the pork, the crab and the lobsters, dress how we want to, it’s okay if a man is with a man. Peter knew that when Paul said we’re not under the law no more, they were gonna struggle with those letters, because they don’t understand that the prophecy was that Christ was going to come and make his soul an offering for sin.

Read it again: nowhere in there did we read that because Christ makes his soul an offering for sin, you no longer have to keep the laws of God. Nowhere did it say that now you can worship another god, or that because he sacrifices himself you don’t have to keep the sabbath day holy, or that now the sabbath is Sunday, or that we all worship the same god and call him different names. Nowhere did it say that you can pray over a pork chop. Nowhere did it say that now all nations could be saved.

“Think not that I am come to destroy the law”: why would he say that? Because Isaiah 53 didn’t mention nothing about him coming to destroy the law. “Or the prophets”: all the prophets never mentioned Christ coming to die to establish another church other than Israel, or to establish that all nations could be saved unto him. “I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil”: to fulfil what was written of him, to die for the people of God, the Israelites.

“For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.” So what in the hell is Christianity talking about, that no longer do we have to keep what they call the civil and judiciary?

There are actually five sets of categories that all the laws fit into: moral, civil, ceremonial, dietary and sacrificial. If you are following a belief that doesn’t even understand that the laws fit into five categories, no way do you know anything about the Bible, and no way do they understand what Paul was teaching. Christianity is telling you that all you got to do is keep the moral. Christ didn’t say that; he said no law shall pass until all be fulfilled.

precepts.why:
Let’s prove it. If you are caught up in that, share this with your brothers, your sisters, your family, because their soul is at stake believing in this replacement theology; eternal salvation is at hand.

“And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life”. The Bible is the book of life; we literally say it, the Bible, the book of life, it tells you about everything. And what happened when the book of life was opened? “And the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.”

The book of life is more than just the moral laws, more than just the New Testament. In Revelation God made sure his people know you will be judged out of the book of life, the entire book. You’re going to be judged on idolatry if you worship another god; if you made graven images, walked around with crosses and idols and prayer beads; if money was your idol, if sex was your idol, if drugs, sports or women was your idol; if you put anything ahead of God. If you took the name of God in vain and lied and blasphemed on him, saying he said this when he didn’t, or saying God justified you to do what he told you not to do, you’re gonna be judged for those things. If you did not keep the sabbath day holy, the seventh day of the week, you’re going to be judged.

Replacement theology telling you all you’ve got to do is keep the moral laws, telling you it don’t matter what religion or what race you are, off of one scripture, maybe two, is damning your soul to eternal damnation. You will be judged based on what’s written in the book of life, the entire Bible.

sense.text: “Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle”: one comma or one period “shall in no wise pass from the law”. All the laws: you can’t worship other gods, you can’t dress how you want to, you can’t eat what you want to, you can’t replace the people of God, “till all be fulfilled.”

“Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments”: the small things, like the dress code; you think it’s small. If you break that commandment “and shall teach men so, he shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven”: that means you won’t be in it. The people in the kingdom will be calling you the least, because you’re out of it. “But whosoever shall do and teach them, the same shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven”: you gotta do and teach the laws of God in the book of life.

This is what happens when you remove the nationality of the people of the book and replace it with a lie, and don’t teach the book of life: our youth are killing each other. When the police show up and scrape the body up off the ground, the age of that boy was 18, the age of that boy was 17, that girl was 16, that boy was 15, that girl was 19. Our brothers the Hispanic brothers, the northern kingdom, are right behind us, because they killing each other too. People don’t even want to go where they think God is, because they know ain’t no truth in it.

The kids are out there on the streets killing each other because the book of life is not being taught, because the damn replacement theology says you ain’t gotta teach nothing but moral laws, and they don’t even teach those. Christians have pulled guns out on brothers in Israel United in Christ; you never had to hold us back from fighting nobody. It’s cause and effect: there are consequences to the lies you follow. It’s gonna be your cousin on a t-shirt, because he don’t want nothing to do with God. Chief Keef is who he follows and idolizes, not King David, not Christ, not Nehemiah, not Ezekiel, not Jeremiah, not Solomon, not the Maccabees.

Why is the church losing so many people? You’re replacing the people of God with everybody. Black kids and Hispanic kids, who are the Israelites, can’t find their identity in the church. They’re not going, so they are finding it in rap music, in Beyoncé’s ungodly … songs, because you’ve replaced them.

A mother stabbed her babies because her baby daddy didn’t want her and was trying to get custody: one is dead and the other is fighting for his life, because you told them the laws of God and the book of life are done away, all you got to do is keep the moral laws, and you don’t even teach those. You can’t teach your people to love their neighbor as they love themselves when they ain’t got no neighbors: they don’t live in neighborhoods, they live in hoods. You can’t teach them that law unless they know that they are the Israelites; that’s the only time that law is effective. Blame Christianity for it.

And it ain’t just the women; it’s across the board, across the country. A father killed his son and himself after claiming his baby mother gave him an STD, because marriage ain’t being taught or pushed in the Christian churches; it’s all feel good. He wasn’t raised from a youth in the law. You got to marry that woman, try to teach her the word of God; you got to repent before something happens, not get an STD, go crazy and kill your son, your flesh and blood.

Our people are sick, and you ain’t helping it in this damn replacement theology. “Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed: how then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?” So we became a strange vine, a degenerate plant, unrecognizable, so degraded morally, physically and spiritually as a people. How did that happen?

precepts.why:
This is how we in today’s time became morally deprived as a people. “Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets”: we found solace, we found comfort in the gangs on the street corners. “As a wild bull in a net: they are full of the fury of the Lord, the rebuke of thy God”: they suffer in the curses of Deuteronomy 28.

Don’t skip, read on: “Therefore hear now this, thou afflicted, and drunken, but not with wine”. We are the afflicted and drunk; we drunk with the lies of replacement theology. “Thus saith thy Lord the Lord, and thy God that pleadeth the cause of his people, Behold, I have taken out of thine hand the cup of trembling, even the dregs of the cup of my fury; thou shalt no more drink it again: But I will put it into the hand of them that afflict thee; which have said to thy soul, Bow down”.

That’s how we became a degenerate plant that kills our own kids. Those that afflicted us said bow down, you not the people of God, “that we may go over”: bow down your soul, you ain’t no better than me, you bleed red like I do. They beat us down, told us we was three-fifths of a man, told us we wasn’t worthy to be the chosen people of God, that we were so bad he went and got a new people, because we were so degenerate a plant that no way you … could rise from the status of being the enslaved people of America; look at what you do to your own kids. They told us to bow our soul down so they can walk over us, and we the chosen people of God.

“And thou hast laid thy body as the ground”: we agreed. “And as the street, to them that went over”: they walked over us. They destroyed our soul in Christianity, destroyed it to the point that we don’t even want to be the people of God; we don’t even want the kingdom of heaven without them in it. That’s a destroyed people right there.

sense.text:
“Beside this he gave them knowledge, and the law of life”: we have the law of life, which is in the book of life, and we have to keep those laws because it is our heritage. We are ingrained with them; we are one and the same with the laws of God. He did not make us to live or conduct our lives without the law.

When we do not have the law, which is our heritage to live by, we become the degenerate plant. We become that ungodly nation that will kill our own people, our own kids. We cannot function without it as a people; we must live by it, or else we will become degenerate. We will digress as a people, we will not progress. It will not happen; we’re not built that way.

That’s why with Christianity we’ve got churches in all of our neighborhoods and we are still destroyed as a people. How is the word of God in the black and Hispanic neighborhoods more than any other race on the face of the earth, and we are still degenerate as a people? Because the law of God is not being taught. We have to keep it.

precepts.why:
Here’s proof that the law is our life and we cannot live without it. That’s the way God made us. Everybody else, they don’t have to live by the words of God; they can do whatever, cause Satan is their god, he’s their father. The God of Israel is our father, and he made it that we cannot live without it and prosper.

“I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death”: life and death is set before us, “blessing and cursing: therefore choose life”. What’s the life and death God is referring to? “That both thou and thy seed may live: That thou mayest love the Lord thy God, and that thou mayest obey his voice”: obey his voice, which is his commandments. “And that thou mayest cleave unto him: for he is thy life”. God is our life, and what did God give us to live by? The commandments. He is our life, the laws are our life; you can’t live without the laws.

“That thou mayest dwell in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them”: that’s who we are. You can’t replace us, because our fathers are Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Yes, we have become a degenerate plant where we are unrecognizable, but God said that degenerate plant will have water placed upon it, and it will grow; it will come back to life.

sense.text:
This is what they forgot: what God said happens to that degenerate plant. We all know how the process of growing plants works. God said we’re a degenerate plant; what do you do to bring back to life a plant that is degrading right before your eyes?

This goes hand in hand with the law of God. The Hebrew religion is the commandments of God, the law of life; if you wanted to know what the Israelites’ religion is, it’s the laws of God. As the book From Babylon to Timbuktu shows, if you deny your religion, the laws of God, you will eventually deny your nationality. You’ll be replaced. You’ll be in the Christian church telling them, I’m not those people of the book, I’m a Gentile, I’m a child of God; we got to keep the laws no more, therefore I’m not Israel. The think tanks know: deny your culture, your heritage, the laws, and over a long period of time you will totally forget your nationality through assimilation. We have forgotten our nationality, and guess what came along: replacement theology. Replacement theology took this as a sign from God that we are not the people of God, not knowing that God would water that degenerate plant again one day.

“For I will take you from among the heathen, and gather you out of all countries, and will bring you into your own land”: we will go back to our own land. America is not our resting place; this is not where we are going to live forever. This place will be destroyed, and God said I’ma take you out, I’ma bring you from that place, because it is destroying you spiritually and physically. That place has told your soul to bow down to the ground: you no longer the people of God, you are nobody, you just gotta believe and have faith, you ain’t chosen; look at what you do, look at how you live, look at your women, look at your man, look at what you eat.

“Then will I sprinkle clean water”: he’s going to sprinkle water on that degenerate plant. The Christian church forgot about this. They didn’t know the prophecies because they didn’t study to show themselves approved. They didn’t know that the degenerate plant nobody could identify, that would do the worst things possible known to man, kill their own kids, worship a white Jesus, God said I will sprinkle water upon them once again. “And ye shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you.”

“A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you”. “And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them.” We’re gonna keep the commandments; we’re going to go back to our way of life.

Before we do that in our own land, you have to rehearse the righteous acts now, to prove yourself worthy of being brought back into that land. Because the land is not going to be some trashed-out hoods; it ain’t gonna be no projects, it ain’t gonna be the filthy streets of Philly, it ain’t gonna be the dirt roads of wherever.

“And ye shall dwell in the land that I gave to your fathers; and ye shall be my people, and I will be your God.” God gonna sprinkle that water back on us, and that’s what he’s doing. That’s why replacement theology won’t stand in the last days when the Israelites come across it. God gonna reveal it to us: cast down this imagination amongst my people, and tell them to raise up their soul from up off the ground. They are greater than what the world has told them they are.

precepts.why: Jump over to verse 35 to show what that land, the land we have to prove ourselves worthy enough to go back to, is going to look like: “This land that was desolate is become like the garden of Eden”. Ain’t even gonna have to work no more for the fruit to grow. You gonna eat the best strawberries, you’re gonna have the best wine, you’re gonna have the best meats; it’s gonna be like the garden of Eden. “And the waste and desolate and ruined cities are become fenced, and are inhabited.”

sense.text:
Now we can walk around with our head held high. We not the …, and the spicks and the baboons and the porch monkeys that the world tell us we are, the Gentiles.

“Thus saith the Lord, which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, which divideth the sea when the waves thereof roar; The Lord of hosts is his name”.

“If those ordinances depart from before me”: if the sun stops shining, the moon stops coming up, the ocean stops going back and forth like it always has since the day God made it, on the second day, the third day, the fourth day. If those things stop, “then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever.” Then we’ll stop. Then you could be justified in replacement theology; then you can say the people of God don’t matter no more, then you can say we all the children of God. If the sun stops shining.

“If heaven above can be measured, and the foundations of the earth searched out beneath, I will also cast off all the seed of Israel for all that they have done”. For all that they have done: that’s what the world thought. The world thought, look at the evil that Israel did, God was so mad at them that he got another people to replace them. All that evil that you read about in the Bible, God said I’m still not going to cast away my people for what they’ve done, still not going to choose another people. You still can’t replace them, because I have not cast them away.

Even with all the evil they have done to become a degenerate plant, they’re no longer in the land, but they still my people, scattered throughout the four corners of the earth. You still can’t replace those people, the sons and daughters of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

precepts.why:
“I say then, Hath God cast away his people?” These are the things the churches don’t read to you, to keep you stupefied in the lies they have brought forth, to keep you doped up on religion. Why would Paul be saying hath God cast away his people? Because he understood the prophecy of Jeremiah: God said I will not cast away my people. So he had to remind them: would God cast away his people for all that they have done, their idolatry? Will he cast away his brothers of the northern kingdom?

“God forbid”: God forbid that he would cast them away and choose another people. “For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.” He’s mentioning who he is, so your race does matter, because God ain’t chosen other people. That’s why he made sure: hey, I’m an Israelite, the seed of Abraham, the tribe of Benjamin, just to let you know God ain’t got another people.
“God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew”: which he’s always known. He did not cast them away.

“Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.” There’s always been a remnant of the Israelites. You can never replace them; God never done away with his people, never.

How can you replace the people of God when Christ himself said he only came for the people of God? This is the prophecy of Christ: “And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.” His people, before he was born; that’s the prophecy on him.
“And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, art not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel.” God’s people has always been Israel.

sense.text:
This is how, when you don’t read the law of God and study to show yourself approved, you will come up with dumb theology like replacement theory. Look what God told Israel before they even moved into the promised land, because he knew there would be a day that people would try to replace his chosen people, his sons and his daughters.

“And the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them”: we scared as hell. “And they shall flee, as fleeing from a sword; and they shall fall when none pursueth.” That’s why they don’t fight no more, they just shoot. “And ye shall have no power to stand before your enemies.”

“And ye shall perish among the heathen, and the land of your enemies shall eat you up. And they that are left of you shall pine away in their iniquity”: the few in number, here in our enemies’ lands. “And also in the iniquities of their fathers shall they pine away with them.”

Because we left off from keeping the commandments, we turned to the ways of the Gentiles, the ways of the other nations. God said that way is going to destroy you, because it is not the law of life; it does not bring life to you. Following the ways of the Gentiles, worshiping and celebrating Christmas and birthdays, brings death to you spiritually and physically.

But look what God said would happen: “If they shall confess their iniquity”, if you admit that those are not the ways of God, that we’ve been living wrong, “and the iniquity of their fathers, with their trespass which they trespassed against me, and that also they have walked contrary unto me”. That means you have to know your race and who you are in order to admit the sins of your fathers that they have done.

“And that I also have walked contrary unto them, and have brought them into the land of their enemies”: that’s through slavery, 1619, the transatlantic slave trade. God did that. “If then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity”: we have not accepted it as a people. That’s why we are in Christianity, trying to find a replacement theology that tells you you don’t have to keep the laws of God, all 600 and something of them; all you got to do is keep the moral.

As long as we are in Christianity as a people, you are telling God that you have not accepted the punishment he has placed upon you. You are looking for loopholes to get to God instead of humbling yourself and keeping the commandments and the faith.
“Then will I remember my covenant with Jacob, and also my covenant with Isaac, and also my covenant with Abraham will I remember; and I will remember the land.” He’s going to remember our ancestors.

precepts.why: “And yet for all that, when they be in the land of their enemies, I will not cast them away”. Before we even went into the promised land, God already cast down replacement theology. He already said that damn supersessionism ain’t gonna work, buddy. I’m gonna tell you right here in Leviticus, I’m never gonna cast away my people, and I’ma remind you throughout the scriptures: I’m going to sprinkle water on that degenerate plant that you can no longer tell is my people. “Neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly, and to break my covenant with them: for I am the Lord their God.”

“But I will for their sakes remember the covenant of their ancestors”: that’s why you got to know your race, cause it’s the covenant of our ancestors. If you don’t know who you are, you will follow the ways of the world, the ways of Christianity, the ways of Satan. It matters who you are, it matters where you come from; you just can’t say I’m a child of God, because God said it’s a covenant of their ancestors, “whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the heathen, that I might be their God: I am the Lord.”

“These are the statutes and judgments and laws, which the Lord made between him and the children of Israel”. It matters that we the children of Israel. You can’t replace us and just say we Gentiles, nor are we looking for an identity that we don’t have, because God already prophesied: I will water that degenerate plant. You may not be able to tell who they are, but I know who they are. They can’t even see themselves anymore, but when I sprinkle that water on them they will begin to realize they are the sons and daughters of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, my chosen people, the house of Israel, and it is time for them to return back to me, because I will never replace them.

That’s the fall of replacement theology: you can’t replace us, because God never replaced us. He made a covenant with us and our ancestors that he would never cast us away, and God is not a man that he should lie. If we are not the Israelites, then what race of people are we in the Bible? If we the Gentiles, which Gentiles are we? The ball is in your court now to prove God wrong, that we not the Israelites.
